result:
I changed the code so the subscription's plan now drives everything that reads a workspace's plan. I ran `tsc --noEmit`, which is clean. I did not run the test suite, and I did not add tests for the changed behaviour.

- **Plan lookups:** `src/server/repositories/organization-repository.ts` now overlays the subscription's plan onto every organization it returns. Workspaces with no subscription record keep the plan stored on the workspace. I did not touch each service individually. Project, issue, seat, invitation, storage and webhook quotas, the feature flags, the switcher and header, and the billing page all read the plan through this repository.
- **Already-broken workspaces:** the overlay is computed on every read, so workspaces whose records already disagree are corrected without anyone changing the plan again.
- **Burst limits:** `src/lib/rate-limit.ts` never learned a workspace's plan. Nothing called `setOrgPlan`, so every workspace was sized as Free. It now looks up the workspace's plan on each call.
- **Trial sweep:** `listTrialsEndingBefore` in `src/server/repositories/subscription-repository.ts` now returns only subscriptions whose status is `trialing`. A workspace that chose a paid plan during its trial (status `active`) is no longer moved to Free. Running the sweep again finds nothing more, because swept subscriptions are then `active` on Free.

I left the plan column on the workspace record alone. A plan change still writes only to the subscription, and reads ignore the column whenever a subscription exists.

When a workspace upgrades, an already-partly-spent rate-limit bucket keeps its remaining tokens. It refills at the new, faster rate, but it isn't topped up to the new capacity straight away.
